title: Streaming Reliability Across Providers, Structured Output, and Agents

effort.rationale: Six distinct user stories spanning provider SSE parsing, structured output metadata handling, disable_streaming logic fixes, agent/graph astream routing, test infra, and release sequencing represent multiple independent, moderately complex fixes across several packages.

impact.rationale: Streaming is a core, widely-used capability and these bugs (hard failures, crashes, silent fallbacks, lost metadata) undermine trust and force workarounds across providers and abstractions, though some issues are reported at low frequency.

title: Enterprise Auth & Transport Security for LangChain Integrations

effort.rationale: Four distinct user stories spanning multiple integrations (ChatAnthropic mTLS, MCP header forwarding, shared httpx layer refactor across providers, SSRF validation hardening) with 6 acceptance criteria implies substantial cross-cutting engineering work.

impact.rationale: Blocks enterprise adoption via proxy/mTLS/PKI requirements and includes a high-severity SSRF security bypass risk, though evidence is thin with mostly single-report frequency across sub-issues.

effort.rationale: Seven distinct user stories spanning provider-specific validation, streaming payload parsing, tool_choice logic, HITL execution gating, observability plumbing, proactive limit warnings, and error-handling unification represent a broad, multi-subsystem effort.

impact.rationale: The gaps span safety-critical human-in-the-loop enforcement, cross-provider reliability, and observability, all of which materially affect developer trust in production agents, though the high-severity risk is scoped to one specific flow.
